source: She didn't finish university. She doesn't have a degree now.
correct: If she had finished university, she would have a degree now.
explanation: Condicional mixta (pasado→presente): <If> + pasado perfecto + <would> + verbo base.

source: He is not very careful. He had an accident last week.
correct: If he were more careful, he wouldn't have had an accident last week.
explanation: Condicional mixta (presente→pasado): <If> + pasado simple + <would have> + participio pasado.

source: We didn't take a map. We got lost.
correct: If we had taken a map, we wouldn't have got lost.
If we had taken a map, we wouldn't have gotten lost.
If we had taken a map, we would not have got lost.
explanation: Tercera condicional: <If> + pasado perfecto + <would(n't) have> + participio pasado.

source: I didn't accept the job offer. Now I regret it.
correct: I wish I had accepted the job offer.
explanation: <Wish> + pasado perfecto expresa arrepentimiento por una decisión pasada.

source: She sold her apartment too cheaply. She's upset about it.
correct: If only she hadn't sold her apartment so cheaply.
explanation: <If only> + pasado perfecto = arrepentimiento intenso por una acción pasada.

source: I don't have a garden. I can't grow vegetables.
correct: If I had a garden, I could grow vegetables.
If I had a garden, I would grow vegetables.
explanation: Segunda condicional: <If> + pasado simple + <would/could> + verbo base para un presente irreal.

source: If we had known about the delay, we would have left later.
correct: Had we known about the delay, we would have left later.
explanation: Inversión condicional formal: <Had> + sujeto + participio pasado reemplaza a <If> + sujeto + pasado perfecto.

source: When water reaches 100°C, it boils.
correct: If water reaches 100°C, it boils.
If you heat water to 100°C, it boils.
explanation: Condicional cero: <If> + presente simple + presente simple para verdades generales.

source: I didn't learn to code. I can't apply for that job now.
correct: If I had learned to code, I could apply for that job now.
explanation: Condicional mixta (pasado→presente): <If> + pasado perfecto + <could/would> + verbo base.

source: What would you do if you lost your passport abroad?
correct: Suppose you lost your passport abroad, what would you do?
Supposing you lost your passport abroad, what would you do?
explanation: <Suppose/Supposing> + pasado simple es una alternativa a <What if> + pasado simple.

source: Without your advice, I would have made a terrible mistake.
correct: But for your advice, I would have made a terrible mistake.
explanation: <But for> + sustantivo = <If it hadn't been for> + sustantivo (formal).

prompt: Change to third conditional with inversion
source: If she hadn't reminded me, I would have forgotten.
correct: Had she not reminded me, I would have forgotten.
explanation: Tercera condicional invertida: <Had> + sujeto + <not> + participio pasado.

source: You can go out if you finish your homework first.
correct: You can go out provided that you finish your homework first.
You can go out provided you finish your homework first.
explanation: <Provided (that)> es una conjunción condicional que significa <only if>.

source: I'll lend you my car if you promise to be careful.
correct: I'll lend you my car as long as you promise to be careful.
explanation: <As long as> = <on condition that>, <provided that>.

source: She is very shy. She didn't speak up at the meeting.
correct: If she weren't so shy, she would have spoken up at the meeting.
If she wasn't so shy, she would have spoken up at the meeting.
explanation: Mixta (presente→pasado): <If> + pasado simple (condición presente) + <would have> + participio pasado (resultado pasado).

source: He studied hard. If he hadn't, he would have failed.
correct: He studied hard. Otherwise, he would have failed.
He studied hard; otherwise, he would have failed.
explanation: <Otherwise> reemplaza una cláusula condicional negativa: <if not> → <otherwise>.

source: If it weren't for his support, I would give up.
correct: Were it not for his support, I would give up.
explanation: Inversión formal: <Were it not for> reemplaza a <If it weren't for>.

source: Maybe she will call. In that case, tell her I'm busy.
correct: If she calls, tell her I'm busy.
explanation: Primera condicional: <If> + presente simple + imperativo/will + verbo base.

source: My roommate leaves dirty dishes everywhere. It annoys me.
correct: I wish my roommate wouldn't leave dirty dishes everywhere.
I wish my roommate would stop leaving dirty dishes everywhere.
explanation: <Wish> + sujeto + <would> expresa frustración por el comportamiento de otros.

source: They didn't check the weather. They got caught in a storm.
correct: If they had checked the weather, they wouldn't have got caught in a storm.
If they had checked the weather, they wouldn't have gotten caught in a storm.
explanation: Tercera condicional: <If> + pasado perfecto + <would(n't) have> + participio pasado.

source: I'll help you if you help me in return.
correct: I'll help you on condition that you help me in return.
explanation: <On condition that> es un equivalente formal de <if>.

source: It might rain, but we'll go hiking anyway.
correct: Even if it rains, we'll go hiking.
explanation: <Even if> expresa que el resultado es el mismo sin importar la condición.

prompt: Change to second conditional with inversion
source: If I were you, I would apologize.
correct: Were I you, I would apologize.
explanation: Inversión formal: <Were> + sujeto reemplaza a <If> + sujeto + <were>.

source: Imagine that you won the lottery. What would you do?
correct: What if you won the lottery?
What if you won the lottery? What would you do?
explanation: <What if> + pasado simple introduce un escenario hipotético de forma informal.

source: He ate too much last night. He feels terrible now.
correct: If he hadn't eaten so much last night, he wouldn't feel terrible now.
explanation: Mixta (pasado→presente): <If> + pasado perfecto + <would(n't)> + verbo base.
